Provides additional buffer-local keymaps for resolving conflicts. #### Keymaps | Key | Action | | -- | -- | | `co` | Keep only ours (top) changes, removing parent (base) part. | | `ct` | Keep only theirs (bottom) changes. | | `cb` | Keep both ours and theirs changes, removing parent part. | | `c0` | Delete the entire conflict block. | | `]x` | Jump to the next conflict start `<<<<<<<`. Supports `vim.v.count`. | | `[x` | Jump to the previous conflict start `<<<<<<<`. Supports `vim.v.count`. | | `]X` | Jump to the first conflict in the file. | | `[X` | Jump to the last conflict in the file. | \* Unlike the motions provided by [mini.bracketed](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.bracketed) keymaps `]x` / `[x` jump only to the start of each conflict `<<<<<<<` — not to every conflict marker `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, or `>>>>>>>`. ### Yapping I tried not to make a mess, but... ### Code

bodyHTML:
About

Features

  1. Enabled only during rebase/merge.
  2. Automatically highlights merge conflicts.
  3. Provides additional buffer-local keymaps for resolving conflicts.

Keymaps

Key Action
co Keep only ours (top) changes, removing parent (base) part.
ct Keep only theirs (bottom) changes.
cb Keep both ours and theirs changes, removing parent part.
c0 Delete the entire conflict block.
]x Jump to the next conflict start <<<<<<<. Supports vim.v.count.
[x Jump to the previous conflict start <<<<<<<. Supports vim.v.count.
]X Jump to the first conflict in the file.
[X Jump to the last conflict in the file.

* Unlike the motions provided by mini.bracketed keymaps ]x / [x jump only to the start of each conflict <<<<<<< — not to every conflict marker <<<<<<<, =======, or >>>>>>>.

Yapping

I tried not to make a mess, but...

Code

Version 1 
local conflict_ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("git_conflict")
local conflict_au = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("git_conflict", { clear = true })

local function minigit_is_merge(buf)
  local git_summary = vim.b[buf].minigit_summary or {}
  local in_progress = git_summary.in_progress or ""
  return in_progress:find("merge") or in_progress:find("rebase")
end

-- get_buf_conflicts(buf) -> { { {1,5}, {3,5}, {5,7} }, ... }
--                               ours   base?  theirs
-- 1: <<<<<<< HEAD
-- 2: local a = "main"
-- 3: ||||||| parent of xxxxxxx (xxx)
-- 4: local a = "base"
-- 5: =======
-- 6: local a = "feature"
-- 7: >>>>>>> xxxxxxx (xxx)
--
local function buf_conflicts(buf)
  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, true)
  local ours, base, theirs = {}, {}, {}
  local conflicts = {}
  local on_end_mark = function()
    local ok = function(val)
      return val[1] and val[2]
    end
    if ok(ours) and ok(theirs) then
      base = ok(base) and base or nil
      table.insert(conflicts, { ours, base, theirs })
      ours, base, theirs = {}, {}, {}
    end
  end
  -- stylua: ignore
  for ln, line in ipairs(lines) do
    if vim.startswith(line, "<<<<<<<") then ours[1] = ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, "|||||||") then base[1] = ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, "=======") then ours[2], base[2], theirs[1] = ln, ln, ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, ">>>>>>>") then theirs[2] = ln; on_end_mark() end
  end
  return conflicts
end

local function conflict_actions()
  local get_prev = function(count)
    count = count or 1
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
    for i = #conflicts, 1, -1 do
      local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflicts[i])
      if lnum > ours[1] then
        if count <= 1 then
          return conflicts[i]
        end
        count = count - 1
      end
    end
  end
  local get_next = function(count)
    count = count or 1
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
    for i = 1, #conflicts, 1 do
      local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflicts[i])
      if lnum < ours[1] then
        if count <= 1 then
          return conflicts[i]
        end
        count = count - 1
      end
    end
  end
  local get_curr = function()
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    for _, conflict in ipairs(vim.b.git_conflicts or {}) do
      local ours, _, theirs = unpack(conflict)
      if lnum >= ours[1] and lnum <= theirs[2] then
        return conflict
      end
    end
  end
  local get_lines = function(from, to)
    return vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, from - 1, to - 1, true)
  end
  local replace = function(conflict, lines)
    local ours, _, theirs = unpack(conflict)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, ours[1] - 1, theirs[2], true, lines)
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ours[1], 0 })
  end
  local jump = function(conflict)
    local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflict)
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ours[1], 0 })
  end
  return {
    ours = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local ours, base, _ = unpack(curr)
        local repl = get_lines(ours[1] + 1, base[1] or ours[2])
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    theirs = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local _, _, theirs = unpack(curr)
        local repl = get_lines(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2])
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    both = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local ours, base, theirs = unpack(curr)
        local repl = {}
        vim.list_extend(repl, get_lines(ours[1] + 1, base[1] or ours[2]))
        vim.list_extend(repl, get_lines(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2]))
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    none = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        replace(curr, {})
      end
    end,
    forward = function()
      local next = get_next(vim.v.count1)
      if next then
        jump(next)
      end
    end,
    backward = function()
      local prev = get_prev(vim.v.count1)
      if prev then
        jump(prev)
      end
    end,
    last = function()
      local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
      local last = conflicts[#conflicts]
      if last then
        local ours, _, _ = unpack(last)
        local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
        if lnum < ours[1] then
          jump(last)
        end
      end
    end,
    first = function()
      local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
      local first = conflicts[1]
      if first then
        local ours, _, _ = unpack(first)
        local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
        if lnum > ours[1] then
          jump(first)
        end
      end
    end,
  }
end

local function conflict_update(buf)
  if not minigit_is_merge(buf) then
    vim.b[buf].git_conflicts = {}
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, conflict_ns, 0, -1)
  else
    local conflicts = buf_conflicts(buf)
    vim.b[buf].git_conflicts = conflicts
    -- Refresh highlights
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, conflict_ns, 0, -1)
    local hi = function(from, to, hl)
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf, conflict_ns, from - 1, 0, {
        end_row = to,
        hl_group = hl,
        hl_eol = true,
      })
    end
    for _, conflict in ipairs(conflicts) do
      local ours, base, theirs = unpack(conflict)
      hi(ours[1], ours[2] - 1, "DiffText")
      if base then
        hi(base[1], base[2] - 1, "DiffDelete")
      end
      hi(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2], "DiffAdd")
    end
  end
end

local conflict_autocmd = function(event, pattern, on_update)
  on_update = on_update or function() end
  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd(event, {
    group = conflict_au,
    pattern = pattern,
    -- stylua: ignore
    callback = function(e) conflict_update(e.buf); on_update(e) end,
  })
end

conflict_autocmd("ModeChanged", "i:*")
conflict_autocmd("TextChanged")
conflict_autocmd("User", "MiniGitUpdated", function(e)
  local buf = e.buf
  -- Just create global keymaps?
  local actions = conflict_actions()
  if minigit_is_merge(buf) then
    vim.keymap.set("n", "co", actions.ours, { buffer = buf, desc = "Checkout ours" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "ct", actions.theirs, { buffer = buf, desc = "Checkout theirs" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "cb", actions.both, { buffer = buf, desc = "Checkout both" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "c0", actions.none, { buffer = buf, desc = "Checkout none" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "]x", actions.forward, { buffer = buf, desc = "Conflict forward" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "[x", actions.backward, { buffer = buf, desc = "Conflict backward" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "]X", actions.last, { buffer = buf, desc = "Conflict last" })
    vim.keymap.set("n", "[X", actions.first, { buffer = buf, desc = "Conflict first" })
  else
    pcall(function()
      vim.keymap.del("n", "co", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "ct", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "cb", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "c0", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "]x", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "[x", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "]X", { buffer = buf })
      vim.keymap.del("n", "[X", { buffer = buf })
    end)
  end
end)

About



Features

Enabled only during rebase/merge.
Automatically highlights merge conflicts.
Provides additional buffer-local keymaps for resolving conflicts.

Keymaps



Key
Action




co
Keep only ours (top) changes, removing parent (base) part.


ct
Keep only theirs (bottom) changes.


cb
Keep both ours and theirs changes, removing parent part.


c0
Delete the entire conflict block.


]x
Jump to the next conflict start <<<<<<<. Supports vim.v.count.


[x
Jump to the previous conflict start <<<<<<<. Supports vim.v.count.


]X
Jump to the first conflict in the file.


[X
Jump to the last conflict in the file.



* Unlike the motions provided by mini.bracketed keymaps ]x / [x jump only to the start of each conflict <<<<<<< — not to every conflict marker <<<<<<<, =======, or >>>>>>>.

local conflict_ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("git_conflict")
local conflict_au = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("git_conflict", { clear = true })

local function minigit_is_merge(buf)
  local git_summary = vim.b[buf].minigit_summary or {}
  local in_progress = git_summary.in_progress or ""
  return in_progress:find("merge") or in_progress:find("rebase")
end

-- get_buf_conflicts(buf) -> { { {1,5}, {3,5}, {5,7} }, ... }
--                               ours   base?  theirs
-- 1: <<<<<<< HEAD
-- 2: local a = "main"
-- 3: ||||||| parent of xxxxxxx (xxx)
-- 4: local a = "base"
-- 5: =======
-- 6: local a = "feature"
-- 7: >>>>>>> xxxxxxx (xxx)
--
local function buf_conflicts(buf)
  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, true)
  local ours, base, theirs = {}, {}, {}
  local conflicts = {}
  local on_end_mark = function()
    local ok = function(val)
      return val[1] and val[2]
    end
    if ok(ours) and ok(theirs) then
      base = ok(base) and base or nil
      table.insert(conflicts, { ours, base, theirs })
      ours, base, theirs = {}, {}, {}
    end
  end
  -- stylua: ignore
  for ln, line in ipairs(lines) do
    if vim.startswith(line, "<<<<<<<") then ours[1] = ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, "|||||||") then base[1] = ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, "=======") then ours[2], base[2], theirs[1] = ln, ln, ln end
    if vim.startswith(line, ">>>>>>>") then theirs[2] = ln; on_end_mark() end
  end
  return conflicts
end

local function conflict_actions()
  local get_prev = function(count)
    count = count or 1
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
    for i = #conflicts, 1, -1 do
      local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflicts[i])
      if lnum > ours[1] then
        if count <= 1 then
          return conflicts[i]
        end
        count = count - 1
      end
    end
  end
  local get_next = function(count)
    count = count or 1
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
    for i = 1, #conflicts, 1 do
      local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflicts[i])
      if lnum < ours[1] then
        if count <= 1 then
          return conflicts[i]
        end
        count = count - 1
      end
    end
  end
  local get_curr = function()
    local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
    for _, conflict in ipairs(vim.b.git_conflicts or {}) do
      local ours, _, theirs = unpack(conflict)
      if lnum >= ours[1] and lnum <= theirs[2] then
        return conflict
      end
    end
  end
  local get_lines = function(from, to)
    return vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, from - 1, to - 1, true)
  end
  local replace = function(conflict, lines)
    local ours, _, theirs = unpack(conflict)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, ours[1] - 1, theirs[2], true, lines)
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ours[1], 0 })
  end
  local jump = function(conflict)
    local ours, _, _ = unpack(conflict)
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ours[1], 0 })
  end
  return {
    ours = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local ours, base, _ = unpack(curr)
        local repl = get_lines(ours[1] + 1, base[1] or ours[2])
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    theirs = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local _, _, theirs = unpack(curr)
        local repl = get_lines(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2])
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    both = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        local ours, base, theirs = unpack(curr)
        local repl = {}
        vim.list_extend(repl, get_lines(ours[1] + 1, base[1] or ours[2]))
        vim.list_extend(repl, get_lines(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2]))
        replace(curr, repl)
      end
    end,
    none = function()
      local curr = get_curr()
      if curr then
        replace(curr, {})
      end
    end,
    forward = function()
      local next = get_next(vim.v.count1)
      if next then
        jump(next)
      end
    end,
    backward = function()
      local prev = get_prev(vim.v.count1)
      if prev then
        jump(prev)
      end
    end,
    last = function()
      local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
      local last = conflicts[#conflicts]
      if last then
        local ours, _, _ = unpack(last)
        local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
        if lnum < ours[1] then
          jump(last)
        end
      end
    end,
    first = function()
      local conflicts = vim.b.git_conflicts or {}
      local first = conflicts[1]
      if first then
        local ours, _, _ = unpack(first)
        local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
        if lnum > ours[1] then
          jump(first)
        end
      end
    end,
  }
end

local function conflict_update(buf)
  if not minigit_is_merge(buf) then
    vim.b[buf].git_conflicts = {}
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, conflict_ns, 0, -1)
  else
    local conflicts = buf_conflicts(buf)
    vim.b[buf].git_conflicts = conflicts
    -- Refresh highlights
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, conflict_ns, 0, -1)
    local hi = function(from, to, hl)
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf, conflict_ns, from - 1, 0, {
        end_row = to,
        hl_group = hl,
        hl_eol = true,
      })
    end
    for _, conflict in ipairs(conflicts) do
      local ours, base, theirs = unpack(conflict)
      hi(ours[1], ours[2] - 1, "DiffText")
      if base then
        hi(base[1], base[2] - 1, "DiffDelete")
      end
      hi(theirs[1] + 1, theirs[2], "DiffAdd")
    end
  end
end

local conflict_autocmd = function(event, pattern, on_update)
  on_update = on_update or function() end
  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd(event, {
    group = conflict_au,
    pattern = pattern,
    -- stylua: ignore
    callback = function(e) conflict_update(e.buf); on_update(e) end,
  })
end

      vim.keymap.del("n", "]X", { buffer = buf })

        vim.keymap.del("n", "]X", { buffer = buf })
        vim.keymap.del("n", "[X", { buffer = buf })
      end
    end
  end,
})

I think `MiniBracketed.conflict` can be a bit difficult to use for conflict checkout, especially since three-way merges aren’t supported due to the `parent` marker `|||||||`.

```
-- 1: <<<<<<< HEAD  
-- 2: -- File 2  
-- 3: ||||||| parent of xxxxxxx (xxx)  
-- 4: -- File 1  
-- 5: =======  
-- 6: -- File 3  
-- 7: >>>>>>> xxxxxxx (xxx)  
```

reply_data.body:
Wow, `toggle_conflicts()` would be a really great feature. But it’s definitely tricky to add new things to `mini.git` without making it too big, since `git` itself already has so many features.

I have a few ideas for how it could work. Not sure if they’re worth it, but I’ll share them anyway.

I really like `vim.b.minigit_summary` because it makes scripting easier. In the same way, conflicts could be stored in a variable like `vim.b.minigit_conflicts` (or added to `vim.b.minigit_summary`).

This variable could be updated from the start, or only after `toggle_conflicts()` is enabled along with highlights. That way, users who only need the data can disable highlights through the `vim.api` and just use the variable. Also, it is too much to include every possible conflict keymap directly in `mini.git`, but having the conflict data available would make it easier for users to build their own mappings.

Maybe `toggle_buf_conflicts()` could simply highlight conflict markers in the current buffer, leaving it up to users to decide when to enable it, for example during a `rebase` or `merge`.

reply_data.body:
> Maybe `toggle_buf_conflicts()` could simply highlight conflict markers in the current buffer, leaving it up to users to decide when to enable it, for example during a `rebase` or `merge`.

Yes, that was the initial idea, same as with `MiniDiff.toggle_overlay(buf_id)`: users themselves toggle the feature when they need it, starting with disabled.

The problem is adding all the machinery of keeping track of text to automatically adjust after conflict markers are added/removed. The 'mini.diff' already has it, so adding overlay is not a huge addition, but it will be for 'mini.git'.

I don't know. But an idea is interesting and I'll keep this in mind. Along with `toggle_line_blame(buf_id)` for an another (surprisingly) popular "show last author of the cursor line" functionality.

reply_data.body: The only issue with `toggle_` function I see is that `MiniGitUpdated` may be triggered multiple times during a `rebase` or `merge`, causing `toggle_conflicts` to repeatedly turn highlights on and off. In *Version 2* (see the original code), I handled this by checking the `vim.b[buf].minigit_conflicts` buffer variable, which can also be used to track whether the overlay is currently enabled for a buffer.
